newsitem.title: UGANDA: Uganda sells 5.0 billion shillings of T-Bills.
newsitem.headline: Uganda sells 5.0 billion shillings of T-Bills.

text.p: Uganda sold all 5.0 billion shillings it tendered in 91-day treasury bills this week, the central Bank of Uganda said on Friday.

It said it sold 4.9352 billion shillings of T-bills at competitive bids and 64.8 million shilling at non-competitive bids. That represented a rise of 566.3 million rise over last week when 4.3689 billion shillings was sold on competitive basis and 4.5 million shillings in a non-competitive package.
The average weighted price stood at 97.401 compared to 97.216 last week while the annualised yield was posted at 10.425 from 11.167 last week.

The bank reported a steady rise in the demand for main category 91-day treasury bills and its offers had risen from 2.0 billion, then to 4.0 billion, 5.0 billion last week and would now be increased to 6.0 billion last week.
Bank officials said the demand for treasury bills could be explained by the increased commercial banks' participation in the market in a bid to reduce investment risks.
Many commercial banks in Uganda suffer from non-performing loans and have resorted to the more secure treasury bills as investment instruments, senior banking sources said.
